The [[1956 Winter Olympics]], officially known as the VII Olympic Winter Games, was an international multi-sport event held in [[Cortina d'Ampezzo]], Italy, from 26 January to 5 February 1956. A total of 821 athletes representing 32 [[National Olympic Committee]]s (NOCs) participated. The games featured 24 events in 4 sports across 8 disciplines.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stillmed.olympics.com/media/Documents/Olympic-Games/Factsheets/The-Olympic-Winter-Games.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221130171949/https://stillmed.olympics.com/media/Documents/Olympic-Games/Factsheets/The-Olympic-Winter-Games.pdf |archive-date=30 November 2022 |date=14 October 2021 |page=2 |title=Factsheet: The Winter Olympic Games |work=[[International Olympic Committee]] |access-date=22 July 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/cortina-d-ampezzo-1956 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240726203236/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/cortina-d-ampezzo-1956 |archive-date=26 July 2024 |access-date=29 July 2024 |title=Cortina d'Ampezzo 1956 Winter Olympics – Athletes, Medals & Results |work=[[International Olympic Committee]] |url-status=live }}</ref>

Overall, athletes from 13 nations received at least one medal, and 9 of them won at least one gold medal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/editions/35 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240715232550/https://www.olympedia.org/editions/35/ |archive-date=15 July 2024 |access-date=23 July 2024 |title=1956 Winter Olympics Overview |work=[[Olympedia]] |url-status=live }}</ref> At their first Winter Olympics, athletes from the [[Soviet Union at the 1956 Winter Olympics|Soviet Union]] won the most gold medals, with 7, and the most overall medals, with 16. Athletes from [[Austria at the 1956 Winter Olympics|Austria]] came second in the medal table with 4 gold medals and 11 medals overall, while athletes from [[Finland at the 1956 Winter Olympics|Finland]] came third with 3 gold medals and 7 medals overall.<ref name=CBC>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/2.722/1956-cortina-d-ampezzo-italy-1.864041 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220809045338/https://www.cbc.ca/sports/2.722/1956-cortina-d-ampezzo-italy-1.864041 |archive-date=9 August 2022 |date=1 December 2009 |work=[[CBC Sports]] |title=1956 Cortina d'Ampezzo, Italy |url-status=live }}</ref> Teams from [[Poland at the 1956 Winter Olympics|Poland]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://olimpijski.pl/olimpijczycy/franciszek-gasienica-gron/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240722153631/https://olimpijski.pl/olimpijczycy/franciszek-gasienica-gron/ |archive-date=22 July 2024 |title=Franciszek Gasienica-Groń (1931–2014) |work=[[Polish Olympic Committee]] |date=24 June 2020 |access-date=22 July 2024 |url-status=live }}</ref> and [[Japan at the 1956 Winter Olympics|Japan]] won their nations' first Winter Olympic medals.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1994039076 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240722170014/https://www.proquest.com/docview/1994039076 |archive-date=22 July 2024 |title=Record medal haul in reach for Japan |work=[[Yomiuri Shimbun#Other publications and ventures|The Japan News]] |id={{ProQuest|1994039076}} |date=6 February 2018 |access-date=22 July 2024}}</ref>

[[Alpine skiing|Alpine skier]] [[Toni Sailer]] of Austria won the most gold medals for an individual at the Games. He won the three gold medals available in the [[Alpine skiing at the 1956 Winter Olympics#Men's events|men's alpine skiing events]] and became the first person to do so.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.latimes.com/local/obituaries/la-me-toni-sailer26-2009aug26-story.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230827235920/https://www.latimes.com/local/obituaries/la-me-toni-sailer26-2009aug26-story.html |archive-date=27 August 2023 |date=26 August 2009 |access-date=23 July 2024 |title=Toni Sailer dies at 73; Austrian skier won all 3 Alpine golds at '56 Olympics |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] }}</ref> [[Cross-country skiing|Cross-country skier]] [[Sixten Jernberg]] of [[Sweden at the 1956 Winter Olympics|Sweden]] won the most overall medals for an individual at the Games, winning four medals with one gold, two silvers, and one bronze.<ref name=CBC /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/athletes/87535 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240429071026/https://www.olympedia.org/athletes/87535 |archive-date=29 April 2024 |title=Sixten Jernberg Biographical information |work=[[Olympedia]] |access-date=29 July 2024 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Medal table==
The medal table is based on information provided by the [[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC) and is consistent with IOC conventional sorting in its published medal tables. The table uses the [[Olympic medal table]] sorting method. By default, the table is ordered by the number of gold medals the athletes from a nation have won. The number of silver medals is taken into consideration next and then the number of bronze medals.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Townsend |first1=Mark |title=US finds its own way to top the medal table at Tokyo Olympics |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2021/aug/07/us-finds-its-own-way-to-top-the-medal-table-at-tokyo-olympics |website=[[The Observer]] |publisher=[[The Guardian]] |access-date=10 July 2024 |date=7 August 2021 |archive-date=17 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240717122912/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2021/aug/07/us-finds-its-own-way-to-top-the-medal-table-at-tokyo-olympics |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=How does the Olympic medal table work? |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/other-sports/athletics/how-olympic-medal-table-work-8647081 |website=[[Daily Mirror]] |date=18 August 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240710191151/https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/other-sports/athletics/how-olympic-medal-table-work-8647081 |archive-date=10 July 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Flanagan |first1=Aaron |access-date=10 July 2024 |language=en }}</ref>

In [[Speed skating at the 1956 Winter Olympics|speed skating]], two gold medals (and no silver) were awarded to [[Yevgeny Grishin (speed skater)|Yevgeny Grishin]] and [[Yuri Mikhaylov]] for a first-place tie in the [[Speed skating at the 1956 Winter Olympics – Men's 1500 metres|men's 1500 metres event]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theatlantic.com/international/archive/2014/02/what-happens-when-olympians-tie-medal/357987/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230601191601/https://www.theatlantic.com/international/archive/2014/02/what-happens-when-olympians-tie-medal/357987/ |archive-date=1 June 2023 |date=12 February 2014 |access-date=23 July 2024 |title=What Happens When Olympians Tie for a Medal? |last1=Ohlheiser |first1=Abby |work=[[The Atlantic]] |url-access=limited |url-status=live }}</ref>
